cards.front: What is the difference between a scalar and a vector quantity?
cards.back:
A **scalar** has **magnitude only** (e.g. mass, speed, energy).
A **vector** has **magnitude and direction** (e.g. displacement, velocity, force).

cards.front: Which SUVAT equation has no time $t$ in it? When can you use it?

cards.back:
The product of **mass and velocity**:
$$p = mv$$
It is a **vector**. Unit: $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ (or $\text{N s}$).

cards.front: State Newton's second law in terms of momentum.
cards.back:
The **resultant force** on a body is **proportional to its rate of change of momentum**, and acts in the **same direction**:
$$F = \dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}$$

cards.front: Define the moment of a force.
cards.back: The product of the **force** and the **perpendicular distance** from the pivot to the **line of action** of the force.

cards.front: Define power. Give the equation for a force moving an object at speed $v$.
cards.back:
Power is the **rate of doing work** (work done per unit time):
$$P = \dfrac{W}{t}$$
For a force $F$ moving an object at speed $v$ in its direction: $P = Fv$.

The ratio of **stress** to **strain**:
$$E = \dfrac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain}} = \dfrac{F/A}{x/L}$$
Use it only within the **limit of proportionality**.

The **charge** that passes a point when a current of **1 A** flows for **1 s**:
$$Q = It$$

The **energy transferred from electrical to other forms per unit charge**:
$$V = \dfrac{W}{Q}$$

The **energy transferred from other forms to electrical energy per unit charge** by the source.
Compare p.d., which is electrical **to other forms**.

cards.front: State Kirchhoff's first law. What is it a consequence of?
cards.back:
The **sum of the currents into a junction** equals the **sum of the currents out**.
It is a consequence of **conservation of charge**.
